report_notes.old: Since `U(s),V(s)` are bounded (uniformly by the fixed-ball bounds), the `O(h^{2\theta})` terms remain `O(h^{2\theta})`.
report_notes.new: For each fixed H and X, U and V are bounded on [0,B], so these terms remain O(h^(2theta)); the U bound is uniform on the fixed H-ball, while the V bound and product-remainder constant may depend on X.
report_notes.contrary_calculation: Take H=0 and X(t)=c t I on a nonzero real Banach space. Then Z=X and V(t)=exp(c t)I; the fixed H-ball K does not bound sup||V|| as c grows. The source makes no uniform-in-X claim about V or the mesh-remainder constant.
report_notes.disposition: Record literal report error without editing the raw report. Its Step2 already supplies Ctheta V for fixed Z, and Step5 gives the correct x-dependent growth. Those public facts suffice for the partition limit with fixed X, while the final constant outside x+x^nu remains theta,B,K-dependent. Therefore this is not a source defect or an absent required product deduction.

counterexample_target_admissibility.source_class: Any nonzero real Banach space X, all zero-initial Ctheta operator paths in B(X), with induced operator norm. There is no compactness, Hamiltonian or actual-driver-range restriction in this target theorem.
counterexample_target_admissibility.identity_example: H=0 and X(t)=c t I are admissible in the actual stated target class; this remains solely a counterexample to the report auxiliary fixed-H-ball bound on V.
counterexample_target_admissibility.optional_compact_driver_variant: If compact drivers were additionally desired, take a nonzero bounded rank-one projection P (or orthogonal rank-one P on Hilbert E) and X(t)=c t P. Then Z=X, V(t)=I+(exp(c t)-1)P, and ||V(t)||>=exp(c t) on Ran(P). Thus even compact perturbation drivers do not give a V bound independent of c.
counterexample_target_admissibility.not_claimed: No assertion that P lies in a particular physical Cameron/force range is needed or made. This is not a new source defect; the target itself imposes no such range restriction.
